title: ClipSAT Course Schema (v2 — blocks model)
description: This top-level shape (a whole course: id + meta + chapters[]) is documentation/illustration ONLY — see the 'examples' block below for a full worked case. What's actually validated file-by-file (scripts/validate-content.js) is #/definitions/courseMeta against content/{track}/_meta.json, and #/definitions/chapter against each content/{track}/{chapter-slug}.json — one chapter per file, per docs/PHASE1-2_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md §2.2, so editing one chapter never requires touching or re-reading a file with every other chapter in it. NOT the format bank-data/*.json question banks use — those have their own ad hoc shape and are intentionally left alone. v2 replaces the original fixed definitions/theorems/keyFormulas/workedExamples split (v1, never adopted) with an ordered blocks[] model, after v1 was found not to match real chapter markup during the WP6 qudrat pilot — see docs/DECISIONS/0002-blocks-model-not-fixed-fields.md.

id.description: Unique kebab-case course identifier matching the filename, e.g. 'digital-sat'.

chapters.description: Ordered list of chapters (topics) in this course.

courseMeta.description: Validates content/{track}/_meta.json — course-level metadata, kept separate from chapter files (one chapter per file, per docs/PHASE1-2_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md §2.2, so no single file needs the whole course read to edit one chapter).

id.description: Unique kebab-case course identifier matching the track slug, e.g. 'digital-sat'.

meta.description: Top-level course metadata displayed on the home card and course header.

title.description: Human-readable course title, e.g. 'Digital SAT Math'.

subtitle.description: Short tagline shown below the title.

prerequisites.description: List of course IDs that are recommended before this course.

color.description: Brand accent colour (hex or CSS variable) — see docs/DESIGN_TOKENS.md, prefer a var(--token).

icon.description: Optional emoji or short string used on the card badge.

estimatedHours.description: Approximate study hours for the full course.

examBoard.description: Awarding body, e.g. 'College Board', 'IB', 'Cambridge'. Proper noun, not translated.

bilingualText.description: Every user-facing string in this schema uses this shape. 'ar': null means not yet translated — render English only, no Arabic toggle for this string. dir="rtl" is derived from the active language at render time, never stored here. HTML/LaTeX allowed inside (matches source markup — e.g. inline \( ... \) math, /, and occasional embedded ... for an Arabic term inside otherwise-English prose).

id.description: Unique slug within the course, e.g. 'qud-about'.

description.description: Optional one-line summary/tag line shown under the title.

quizWidget.description: NOT quiz question data — every chapter's 'Chapter Quiz' section is a live widget (count/level selectors + a Generate button, genChapterQuiz() in engine.js) that pulls from bank-data/{track}.json at request time. This just tells the template whether to render that widget for this chapter.

chapterContent.description: All instructional material for a chapter, as an ORDERED sequence of blocks — order matters and is preserved from the source (unlike a v1-style split into separate definitions[]/theorems[]/etc. arrays, which loses document flow).

videos.description: Embedded topic videos (Appendix A benchmark task 6 — see docs/RECIPES.md #6).

provider.description: Extend this enum if a second provider is ever needed — don't add a differently-shaped field.

videoId.description: The provider's video ID (e.g. YouTube's 11-char ID), not a full URL.

topicTag.description: Optional free-text tag linking this video to a specific block by id.

explorers.description: References ONLY — the canvas drawing/interaction code stays in public/js/engine.js, keyed by canvasId. This array just tells a template where to mount an explorer and what to call it. Does not duplicate or reimplement any of the 56 existing canvas explorers (docs/INVENTORY.md §A).

canvasId.description: Must match an id engine.js's explorer-mounting code already recognizes — this schema does not create new explorer behavior.

type.description: Explorer category, e.g. 'function-explorer', 'riemann-sum' — matches engine.js's existing type strings.

block.description: A discriminated union on 'kind'. Kinds were derived from what real chapter markup actually contains (grep counts across index.html as of WP6, docs/DECISIONS/0002): 'callout' covers definition/theorem/note/warning/proof/worked-example boxes (489+398 real instances — they all share one label+body shape, differing only in a style class), 'table' (22 instances, e.g. an exam section map), 'cards' (212 instances, e.g. a Format/Calculator/Skills/Signature stat grid), and 'text' for a plain paragraph with no wrapper.

style.description: def=definition, thm=theorem/rule, note=informational, warn=practice problem or caution, pf=proof, example=worked example, tip=study-strategy tip. Maps to a template-owned CSS class — content authors pick a semantic style, not a class name.

label.description: Optional heading line, e.g. 'Definition — Antiderivative' or 'What to expect'. Many callouts have one; not all.

body.description: Main prose. LaTeX allowed (\( \) inline, \[ \] display).

copyLatex.description: Optional: if this callout has a 'Copy LaTeX' button (rare — 7 instances sitewide as of WP6), the LaTeX string it copies. Math notation, not translated.

subtitle.en: Quantitative reasoning for Qiyas's General Aptitude Test

body.en: The General Aptitude Test (GAT — القدرات العامة, "Qudrat") is administered by Qiyas. Alongside a verbal section it has a quantitative section that measures reasoning with numbers rather than memorised content.
body.ar: يُدار اختبار القدرات العامة (GAT) من قِبل المركز الوطني للقياس ("قياس"). إلى جانب القسم اللفظي، يضم الاختبار قسمًا كمّيًا يقيس التفكير المنطقي بالأرقام بدلاً من المحتوى المحفوظ.

body.en: Questions are multiple choice and are answered without a calculator, so speed and clean mental methods matter as much as the mathematics.
Estimate before computing; keep fractions instead of converting to decimals where possible.
A student answers 36 out of 45 questions correctly. What percentage is that? <details><summary>Show solution</summary>80%.</details>
